text: To the angel of the church in Ephesus: he who holds the seven stars and walks among the seven lampstands says this.
He knows their works, hard work and endurance, that they cannot bear evil people, and that they tested false apostles and found them liars.
They have endured and borne up for his name without growing weary.
But he has this against them: they have abandoned the love they had at first.
They must remember how far they have fallen, repent and do the first works, or he will come and remove their lampstand.
Yet they hate the works of the Nicolaitans, as he does.
Whoever has an ear should hear what the Spirit says; to the one who conquers he will give the tree of life in God's paradise.
To the angel in Smyrna: the first and the last, who died and came to life, says this.
He knows their suffering and poverty, though they are rich, and the slander of those who falsely claim to be Jews but are a synagogue of Satan.
They should not fear coming suffering: the devil will jail some of them for a test, with ten days of trouble. Be faithful even to death and receive the crown of life.
Whoever has an ear should hear; the one who conquers will not be hurt by the second death.
To the angel in Pergamum: he who has the sharp double-edged sword says this.
He knows they live where Satan's throne is, yet hold his name and did not deny the faith even when Antipas, his faithful witness, was killed among them.
But he has a few things against them: some hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to trip Israel into eating idol food and sexual sin.
Likewise some hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
So they must repent, or he will come quickly and fight against them with the sword of his mouth.
Whoever has an ear should hear; the conqueror gets hidden manna and a white stone with a new name written on it that only the receiver knows.
To the angel in Thyatira: the Son of God, whose eyes blaze like fire and whose feet are like bronze, says this.
He knows their love, faith, service and endurance, and that their recent works exceed their first.
But he has this against them: they tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophet and misleads his servants into sexual sin and eating idol food.
He gave her time to repent, but she refuses to turn from her immorality.
So he will throw her onto a sickbed, and those who join her into great suffering unless they repent of her ways.
Her children he will strike dead, so all the churches will know that he searches minds and hearts and repays each according to their works.
To the rest in Thyatira who do not hold her teaching he puts no other burden on them,
only that they hold fast to what they have until he comes.
To the one who conquers and keeps his works to the end, he will give authority over the nations,
to rule them with an iron rod like a potter's vessels broken, just as he received from his Father;
and he will give that person the morning star.
Whoever has an ear should hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
